title: Nationwide Emergency Alert Test Today at 1:20 p.m. — TV and Radio Only, No Action Needed
excerpt: FEMA and the FCC will test the Emergency Alert System nationwide at about 1:20 p.m. Central today, Tuesday, Nov. 17. TV and radio will pause for about a minute. Your phone will not go off, and no action is needed.
content:
The Federal Emergency Management Agency, working with the Federal Communications Commission, will conduct a nationwide test of the Emergency Alert System at about 1:20 p.m. Central Time today, Tuesday, November 17, 2026. Radio and television programming across the country — including here in Laredo — will pause briefly for the test message.

The test is routine and required by federal law at least once every three years. It is the first nationwide test since October 2023. The message will say: “This is a nationwide test of the Emergency Alert System, issued by the Federal Emergency Management Agency. This is only a test. No action is required by the public.” It will go out in English and Spanish and last about a minute.

Your cellphone will not go off. Unlike the October 2023 test, today’s exercise covers TV and radio only — broadcast, cable, satellite and radio. No Wireless Emergency Alert will be sent to phones.

FEMA has pushed back on online rumors tying the test to a nationwide blackout or a secret emergency, saying plainly: “No blackouts, no secret emergencies.” No federal agency, utility or grid operator has announced a blackout, and the test does not touch the power grid or the internet.

If severe weather or a real emergency forces a postponement, the backup date is Thursday, December 3, at the same time.

Source: FEMA, 2026 Nationwide Emergency Alert System Test; FCC Public Notice DA 26-989, Sept. 16, 2026.

Webb Watch 956
